ocar.opportunity: Forward locomotion in C. elegans is a tractable behavior whose generating circuit can be studied on a mapped connectome that includes chemical synapses, gap junctions, and peptides.
ocar.challenge: Which neurons belong to the locomotory subnetwork, how their activity becomes traveling muscle waves, and which cells are necessary for coordination were not identified in a multilayer-network plus control-theoretic setting.
ocar.action: Maertens, Schöll, Ruiz, and Hövel (Neurocomputing 2020; this extract is arXiv:2006.08771) build a multilayer network over transmitters and peptides, predict locomotory neurons by logistic regression, simulate Hindmarsh–Rose neurons with leaky-integrator muscles, and apply time-delayed feedback.
ocar.resolution: They predict a locomotory subnetwork, model forward motion as harmonic waves, report a network-based central pattern generator, and show that feedback increases synchronicity. Silencing analyses identify high-impact motor neurons; without silencing, a time-averaged order parameter of 70.1% is the reference, with lower values after silencing groups such as VA12 (60.6% in the figure).
ocar.future_work: Locomotion is simulated, not measured on worms in this extract. The claim that information processing is the same in humans and C. elegans is analogical. Catalog pdf_chars_body is abnormally large, suggesting a messy extract; numbers used here are those visible in the selected text only.

summaries.beginner: The worm’s walking circuit can be drawn as stacked networks of different chemical signals. This modeling paper picks likely walking neurons, simulates their rhythms, and tests which cells, when silenced in the model, break coordinated muscle waves.
summaries.intermediate: The PDF extract is an arXiv preprint (2006.08771, June 2020) of Maertens, Schöll, Ruiz, and Hövel’s Neurocomputing paper. They treat the C. elegans connectome as a multilayer network, use logistic regression to predict locomotory neurons, and couple Hindmarsh–Rose activity to a leaky muscle model and harmonic-wave locomotion. Time-delayed feedback is used to enhance wave synchronicity; appendix figures report a 70.1% reference order parameter and drops when DA, DB, VA, or VD neurons are silenced in combination. Highlights claim a network-based CPG.
summaries.advanced: This is computational neuroscience, not a new reconstruction. “Proof of a network-based CPG” is an author highlight. The 70.1% order parameter and silencing percentages are from model figures in the extract, not behavioral experiments. Human-equivalence of information processing is not evidenced here. The input’s pdf_chars_body field is implausibly large (~25 million); pedagogical text uses only the provided pdf_text/abstract.

plain_language_summary: The worm’s walking circuit can be drawn as stacked networks of different chemical signals. This modeling paper picks likely walking neurons, simulates their rhythms, and tests which cells, when silenced in the model, break coordinated muscle waves.

ocar.opportunity: Connectomes appear genetically encoded, but a general, experimentally testable map from neuronal expression patterns to wiring rules was missing.
ocar.challenge: Measurement noise, spatial constraints, and combinatorial gene interactions make it hard to invert adjacency matrices into molecular interaction rules.
ocar.action: Kovács, Barabási, and Barabási post on bioRxiv (2020) a connectome model linking the adjacency matrix to neuronal expression, applied first to C. elegans gap junctions.
ocar.resolution: They infer a network of 19 innexin interactions governing gap-junction formation, five of which are already supported by experimental data. The framework is set up to extend to chemical synapses via a directed model B = X O Y and a geometric reading of the wiring-rule matrix O.
ocar.future_work: Chemical-synapse search currently spans the genome; adult transcription-factor expression may not reflect developmental history. The authors prioritize experimental validation of homomeric gap-junction rules before expanding the chemical-synapse basis. Catalog lists PNAS as journal; this extract is the bioRxiv preprint.

summaries.beginner: If each neuron’s gene list is its identity card, there should be rules for which cards are allowed to form a connection. This paper infers such rules for worm gap junctions from wiring plus innexin expression.
summaries.intermediate: Posted on bioRxiv (5 May 2020), Kovács, D. L. Barabási, and A.-L. Barabási introduce a computational framework that ties connectome adjacency to expression profiles while allowing for noise and spatial restrictions. For C. elegans gap junctions they infer 19 innexin interactions, five already experimentally supported. Later sections set up a directed connectome model for chemical synapses and interpret wiring rules as a pseudo-metric in expression space, arguing that a diagonal (shared-gene) rule is too weak for combinatorial synapse formation. Significance text in the catalog frames experimentally falsifiable genetic encoding of links.
summaries.advanced: Nineteen rules and five validated interactions are author-reported inferences, not a full experimental screen in this paper. Chemical-synapse inversion is formulated, not solved with a complete O matrix in the selected extract. Catalog journal is PNAS while DOI/PDF are bioRxiv (later published in PNAS). Spatial embedding and Minkowski-like geometry remarks are theoretical interpretation.

plain_language_summary: If each neuron’s gene list is its identity card, there should be rules for which cards are allowed to form a connection. This paper infers such rules for worm gap junctions from wiring plus innexin expression.

ocar.opportunity: Mechanisms that specify neuronal diversity are well known; whether those same spatial, temporal, and hemilineage programs also specify circuit assembly was unclear.
ocar.challenge: Linking developmental origin to synapse-level connectivity required identifying the same cells in a TEM volume without biasing toward a particular projection pattern.
ocar.action: Mark, Lai, Zarin, Manning, Pollington, Litwin-Kumar, Cardona, Truman, and Doe in eLife (2021) map 160 interneurons from seven bilateral neuroblasts into a synapse-scale TEM reconstruction of the Drosophila larval CNS.
ocar.resolution: Lineages concurrently build sensory and motor neuropils via Notch-dependent hemilineages that share synaptic targeting, further refined by temporal identity. Hemilineage-temporal cohorts share connectivity beyond what proximity predicts. In all lineages examined, NotchON hemilineages projected to dorsal/motor neuropil and NotchOFF to ventral/sensory neuropil.
ocar.future_work: The seven neuroblasts were chosen by clone success and Gal4 availability. Whether NotchON always maps to motor neuropil for all ~30 segmental neuroblasts is open. Testing spatial identity would require duplicating a neuroblast and comparing projections. Catalog year 2019 is the project era; the PDF is eLife 2021.

summaries.beginner: Fruit-fly nerve-cord cells remember which stem cell they came from, which sister they are, and when they were born. This paper finds those developmental labels still show up in where synapses sit and who talks to whom.
summaries.intermediate: In eLife (2021), Mark, Doe and colleagues identify 160 interneurons from seven bilateral neuroblasts in a larval Drosophila TEM reconstruction. Notch-dependent hemilineages split motor versus sensory neuropil targeting; temporal identity refines synapse localization; connectome analysis shows shared connectivity in hemilineage-temporal cohorts that proximity cannot explain. Discussion contrasts this with mammalian clones that often share location and morphology: fly neuroblast clones project broadly yet stereotypically. NotchON consistently went dorsal/motor and NotchOFF ventral/sensory in every lineage tested here.
summaries.advanced: n = 160 cells from 14 hemilineages (seven bilateral neuroblasts), not the whole nerve cord. Selection by Gal4/clone availability could still bias morphology despite the authors’ argument to the contrary. “Broadly applicable throughout the nervous system” is a concluding claim, not a whole-CNS test. Proximity controls are reported as insufficient; the extract does not quote the statistical test. Catalog year 2019 disagrees with the 2021 publication date on the PDF.
